result.topic_en: Euler derives the parameter of the parabola through points F and H from a quadratic equation, notes that no such curve exists unless fh > gg, and observes that when fh > gg two quite different parabolas both satisfy the minimum condition, which he proposes to examine further.

vero $v$ statim erit $g = -\sqrt{af-aa} + \sqrt{ah-aa}$, sive
$g+\sqrt{af-aa} = \sqrt{ah-aa}$; unde sumtis quadratis fit $gg+2g\sqrt{af-aa}$
$+af-aa = ah-aa$, sive $2g\sqrt{af-aa} = a(h-f)-gg$, iterumque
quadrando $4gg(af-aa) = aa(h-f)^2 - 2agg(h-f) + g^4$, sive
$aa((h-f)^2+4gg) - 2agg(h+f) + g^4 = 0$. Pro hujus
aequationis solutione ponamus $a = \frac{gg}{z}$, ut habeamus
$0 = zz - 2(h+f)z + (h-f)^2 + 4gg$, unde fit
$z = (h+f) + 2\sqrt{hf-gg}$, ideoque $a = \frac{gg}{h+f+2\sqrt{fh-gg}}$.

items.quote:
Hinc jam statim patet, nisi fuerit $fh > gg$
curvam quaesitam esse imaginariam, sive his casibus nul-
lam curvam per puncta F et H traduci posse
items.english: Hence it is immediately clear that unless fh > gg, the sought curve is imaginary, i.e. in these cases no curve can be drawn through the points F and H.

items.quote:
ita ut hinc natura minimi neutiquam excludi
posse videatur
items.english: so that the nature of a minimum does not at all seem to be excludable from this.

items.english: Because of the ambiguous sign of the radical, two parabolas passing through F and H can be exhibited, both of which have the character of a minimum, although they differ greatly from each other.
